_README: DEF-263 — template for appsettings.Secrets.json, the server-only secrets overlay.
WHAT THIS IS FOR
Every other config file the app reads ships inside the deploy zip, so a secret written into
one of them on the server is destroyed by the next extract. Worse, it fails SILENTLY: empty
SMTP credentials make Program.cs fall back to MockEmailService, which logs the message and
delivers nothing, so 2FA codes and password-reset links simply stop arriving with no error.
appsettings.Secrets.json is excluded from the publish output (GCCWebApp.csproj) and from git
(.gitignore), and Scripts/deploy.ps1 ABORTS if it ever reaches the staging folder. Because it
is absent from the zip it survives every deploy: extracting adds and overwrites, never deletes.
HOW TO USE IT
1. Copy this file to appsettings.Secrets.json in the SAME folder as GCCWebApp.dll
on the server (the site root, alongside appsettings.Production.json).
2. Fill in the real values and delete every _README / _comment key.
3. Recycle the application pool.
Keep this file OUT of source control and out of deploy zips. It is loaded last, so anything
here overrides appsettings.json and appsettings.Production.json. Environment variables still
outrank it.
SMTP NOTES FOR THE GCC MAIL SERVER
Only Username and Password belong here. Host, port and transport are non-secret and already
set in appsettings.Production.json — but two of those values are load-bearing and easy to
'correct' into a broken state:
Host must be accumail3.accuwebhosting.com, NOT mail.gccwebapp.com. Both resolve to the same
IP (72.18.135.96), but the server's TLS certificate only covers the accuwebhosting name, so
the friendlier-looking host fails certificate validation before it ever authenticates.
Port must be 465 with Security=SslOnConnect. Port 587 advertises no STARTTLS and answers an
explicit STARTTLS with '503 TLS is not allowed', so 465 is the only encrypted path.
THE ONLY MAILBOX THAT EXISTS IS admin@gccwebapp.com
Verified 2026-08-19 by SMTP RCPT probe: admin@ is accepted; noreply@, no-reply@, support@ and
info@ all return '550 No such user here', and an invented control address is rejected too, so
the server does real per-user validation. FromEmail is therefore admin@gccwebapp.com. If a
friendlier sender is wanted later, create the mailbox or alias FIRST - setting FromEmail to an
address that does not exist invites rejection at the server and bounced replies.
